title: Run AI production experiment
description:
## Context

Parent tracker for evolving pdf_viewer through mostly hands-off agent work on experimental branches while keeping main as the stable baseline.

## What to build

Coordinate the experiment through Beads, repo-owned docs, and narrow agent-ready slices.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Work is tracked in beads rather than TODO.md
- [ ] Agent sessions start from br ready and docs/ai-production.md
- [ ] Main remains a stable baseline until work is intentionally merged

## Verification

Run br ready and confirm child beads are independently actionable.

title: Reproduce and fix Cmd-F failure on large sections
description:
## Context

Native Cmd-F is unreliable on large converted PDFs. The user reports several failure modes: sometimes Cmd-F cannot find text until a hard reload (Cmd-Shift-R), sometimes it finds too many or wrong entries, and pressing Enter can move to an adjacent page without the expected highlighted text visible. TODO.md also says Cmd-F works for small sections but not large sections. ADR 0009 says full-document native find depends on .pf content-visibility: auto and avoiding display:none page gating.

## What to build

Reproduce the native-find failure on a large cached or freshly converted PDF, identify whether the cause is stale injected assets, content-visibility behavior, text-layer ordering, page virtualization, browser find interaction, or reload/cache state, and restore reliable native Cmd-F over large PDFs. Preserve the content-visibility architecture unless evidence requires a new ADR.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A large cached or freshly converted PDF reproduces at least one reported failure mode before the fix
- [ ] Cmd-F can find text beyond the initially visible/small section after the fix
- [ ] Enter/cycling in browser find scrolls to a visible native highlight, not an adjacent blank/wrong page
- [ ] The fix does not reintroduce display:none text gating or the deleted surrogate shadow text layer
- [ ] docs/keybindings.md or ADR notes are updated if behavior or architecture changes

## Verification

Use the real daemon at localhost:7435 with a large converted PDF. Verify native Cmd-F finds terms outside the initially visible pages, survives normal reload state, and does not require Cmd-Shift-R to start working.

title: Fix visual-mode next-page navigation when j/k fails but repeated w works
description:
## Context

In visual mode, the user sometimes has to press w repeatedly to advance while j/k does not move to the next page. This breaks the expected vertical reading/navigation model.

## What to build

Find why visual-mode j/k cannot cross certain page/text-layer boundaries and make vertical movement advance predictably to the next logical line/page.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Reproduce a case where w w w advances but j j j does not
- [ ] j/k can move through the same boundary without getting stuck
- [ ] The fix respects text ordering and does not create jumps to unrelated figure/caption layers

## Verification

On a converted PDF with the failure mode, enter visual mode and verify j/k can move through the problematic boundary.

title: Decide the minimum ergonomic pins interaction
description:
## Context

Pins/markers are one of the most important product directions. The user wants to drop a location, keep working, jump back quickly, and open a nimble overview of all pins. The design should reference docs/pins.md.

## What to build

Turn docs/pins.md into a concrete first-version interaction contract: terminology, commands, menu shape, ordering, persistence scope, and how it relates to Vimium marks. This is a HITL design bead, not an implementation bead.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] docs/pins.md is updated with the chosen MVP interaction
- [ ] The first version defines how to drop a pin, jump to the latest pin, list pins, and title pins from selected text
- [ ] The design decides whether persistence is in-tab only or cross-session for V1
- [ ] The design decides whether pins use letters, numbers, recency, or explicit names
- [ ] Follow-up implementation beads are updated if the chosen design changes them

## Verification

User reviews docs/pins.md and confirms the MVP interaction before implementation starts.

title: Implement MVP pin drop and jump-back flow
description:
## Context

After the pins interaction is decided in docs/pins.md, implement the smallest useful flow: drop a pin at the current reading location and jump back to it quickly.

## What to build

Implement the chosen V1 from docs/pins.md for dropping a pin and returning to the most recent or selected pin. Keep the implementation easy to revise after user testing.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A user can drop a pin at the current page/viewport anchor
- [ ] If text is selected and the design says to use it, that text becomes the default pin title
- [ ] A user can jump back to the most recent/current pin with the chosen command
- [ ] No undocumented keybinding conflicts are introduced
- [ ] docs/keybindings.md and docs/pins.md are updated

## Verification

Open a converted PDF, drop a pin, move elsewhere, use the chosen command to jump back, and confirm the viewport returns to the pinned location.

title: Implement keyboard-first pins overview
description:
## Context

The user wants a nimble overview of all pins with page number, chapter, quote/title, and possibly a page thumbnail. This should follow the decided interaction in docs/pins.md.

## What to build

Add the chosen pins overview/menu. It should be keyboard-navigable, semantic/Vimium-hintable, and optimized for recognizing and jumping to pins quickly.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The overview lists all pins for the current document
- [ ] Each row shows page number and title/quote; chapter is shown when available
- [ ] Keyboard navigation and Enter selection work
- [ ] Controls are real buttons or otherwise Vimium-hintable
- [ ] docs/pins.md documents the final V1 overview behavior

## Verification

Create multiple pins, open the overview, navigate between rows by keyboard, and jump to each pin.

title: Implement homepage search index for all cached PDFs
description:
## Context

The user wants a single shortcut target: a pretty, minimal homepage/search index for the PDF viewer, not itself a PDF, showing all/recent PDFs and a Command-K-like navigation experience. This overlaps with the existing daemon /library and visit tracking.

## What to build

Add a daemon-served homepage/index page that lists recent/cached PDFs and supports fast keyboard search/open. Use the existing visual language where possible and keep it minimal and clean.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A stable URL opens the PDF viewer homepage/index without requiring a PDF path
- [ ] The page lists recently used and/or cached PDFs from existing daemon/library data
- [ ] Search/filter is keyboard-first and can open a selected PDF
- [ ] The page is suitable for mapping to a browser/app shortcut
- [ ] README.md documents the homepage URL and shortcut use

## Verification

Start or use the real daemon, open the homepage URL, search for a known cached PDF, press Enter, and land in that PDF viewer page.

title: Add a native-PDF fallback command
description:
## Context

When text rendering is bad, the user wants an easy toggle/key/palette command to open the same PDF natively instead of deleting cache entries or using hard reload workarounds. The viewer already has passthrough behavior for cache misses and stores source data for some conversions.

## What to build

Add an explicit command that opens the current PDF in the browser/native PDF viewer or original source. Audit whether every cached entry has enough original path/URL/source PDF information; if not, add the smallest source-metadata/copy behavior needed for reliable fallback.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The current viewer exposes a command/palette entry to open the native PDF
- [ ] Local PDFs and remote cached PDFs both have a defined fallback behavior
- [ ] The command does not require deleting cache entries
- [ ] Redirect loops are avoided using the existing passthrough mechanism or an equivalent safe marker
- [ ] docs/keybindings.md and docs/cache.md are updated if commands/cache semantics change

## Verification

Open a cached converted PDF, trigger the native fallback command, and confirm the browser opens the corresponding native PDF surface instead of the custom HTML viewer.

title: Research Comet LLM access to viewer context
description:
## Context

The north star is a PDF viewer optimized for LLM context. Comet has an LLM sidebar that can inspect or fetch some text from pages. We need to know what it can access from the converted viewer and whether the viewer should expose an llms.txt-like layer, current viewport endpoint, or full-document text endpoint.

## What to build

Run a focused investigation of what the Comet LLM sidebar can see from the viewer: DOM text, selected text, current viewport, same-origin daemon endpoints, and linked resources. Then propose the smallest context surface that gives the LLM both the whole document and an ergonomic take on what the user is seeing now.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Document what Comet LLM can and cannot access from a served PDF viewer page
- [ ] Determine whether it can fetch additional localhost URLs linked from the page
- [ ] Propose whether to expose full-document text, current viewport text, selected text, and/or llms.txt-style metadata
- [ ] Identify privacy/localhost constraints and failure modes
- [ ] Create follow-up implementation beads if the proposed surface is accepted

## Verification

Use a real converted PDF in Comet and record observed LLM sidebar behavior, including exact prompts or tests used.

title: Profile and reduce memory use for large books
description:
## Context

Opening a large book can consume around 2 GB of memory in the browser tab, which is not feasible as a normal reading workflow. Possible causes include pdf2htmlEX image layers, page rendering, content-visibility behavior, retained thumbnails, or asset caching.

## What to build

Measure memory use on a representative large cached book, identify the dominant contributors, and implement the smallest safe reduction. Preserve native find and text selection unless a documented tradeoff is explicitly accepted.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Establish a repeatable before/after memory measurement method
- [ ] Identify the main memory contributors for a large book
- [ ] Reduce memory usage meaningfully or document why the first safe reduction is blocked
- [ ] Native Cmd-F and text selection still work after the change
- [ ] Any architectural tradeoff is captured in docs/adr/ or a follow-up bead

## Verification

Open the same large cached book before and after the change and compare browser tab memory using the chosen repeatable measurement method.

title: Normalize logical text order for search and visual navigation
description:
## Context

pdf2htmlEX text layers can be ordered illogically. Vimium-style navigation, overlay search, and visual-mode j/k can jump up/down when figure or diagram text appears in a different layer/order than the visual reading order. Forking pdf2htmlEX is a future track; first investigate what can be fixed in this repo.

## What to build

Research and prototype a repo-local way to derive visual/logical text order from positions instead of raw DOM order. Apply it only where it improves overlay search/selection/navigation without breaking native browser find.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Identify at least one PDF/page where current order jumps illogically
- [ ] Document whether the fix belongs in overlay code, injection/post-processing, or future pdf2htmlEX work
- [ ] Prototype or implement a narrow order-normalization path for overlay-controlled features
- [ ] Native browser find is not regressed

## Verification

On the repro PDF, use overlay search or visual j/k before and after; confirm movement follows visual reading order better.

title: Show only top-level chapters in header and make sidebar hierarchy navigable
description:
## Context

When a PDF has several layers of chapters, the header should prefer top-level chapters. The left menu should behave more like a collapsible hierarchy so lower-level entries are available without overwhelming the main chapter signal.

## What to build

Adjust outline/chapter presentation so the header uses top-level chapter context, while the sidebar can show nested chapters with collapse/expand behavior.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Header/current chapter display prefers top-level outline entries when nesting exists
- [ ] Sidebar preserves access to nested entries
- [ ] Nested groups can be collapsed/expanded by keyboard and pointer
- [ ] Outline controls remain semantic/Vimium-hintable
- [ ] docs/keybindings.md is updated if new commands are added

## Verification

Open a PDF with nested outline entries and confirm the header shows top-level context while the sidebar supports navigating nested entries.

title: Codify AI production docs and Beads setup
description:
## Context

Bootstrap the experiment branch with Beads and a repo-local documentation contract.

## What to build

Initialize .beads, add Beads agent guidance, document doc ownership, and mark TODO.md as legacy intake.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] .beads is initialized with git-tracked JSONL state
- [ ] CLAUDE.md / AGENTS.md point agents at the workflow
- [ ] README.md points to the workflow doc
- [ ] TODO.md no longer presents itself as the active backlog

## Verification

br agents --check, br sync --status, and git diff --check.

title: Polish keybinding hint icon styling and Cmd-K copy
description:
## Context

The small icons for keybinds should be slightly darker/more anonymous. The Command-K UI copy should also remove the em dash. This is a narrow visual/text polish task.

## What to build

Adjust the keybinding icon styling by a small amount toward darker grey and remove the em dash from the Command-K copy. Keep the UI quiet and consistent with the existing viewer style.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Keybinding icons render darker/more anonymous without becoming too low-contrast
- [ ] The Command-K surface no longer uses an em dash in the targeted copy
- [ ] No unrelated palette text is rewritten

## Verification

Open the relevant overlay/palette UI and visually confirm the keybinding icons and Command-K copy.

title: Hide page-number Command-K action when unsupported
description:
## Context

The Command-K page-number action should not appear for documents where page numbers are not supported or cannot be mapped correctly. Unsupported commands create dead ends in the palette.

## What to build

Detect whether page-number navigation is supported for the current document and hide or disable the Command-K page-number action when it is not valid. Prefer hiding unless the UI has a clear disabled-state convention.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Documents without supported page-number mapping do not show a usable page-number command
- [ ] Documents with supported page-number mapping still show and execute the command
- [ ] The condition is based on document capability, not a hardcoded filename

## Verification

Open one document with page-number support and one without, then compare Command-K results.

title: Add navigation undo for accidental movement
description:
## Context

The user wants a Cmd-Z-style way to revert accidental movement. This should restore recent viewport/page movement, not undo text edits. It is especially useful when find/selection/navigation unexpectedly moves the reader.

## What to build

Add a small navigation history stack and a command to return to the previous reading position. Choose the key/palette shape according to docs/keybindings.md constraints.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The viewer records meaningful reading-position changes without recording every tiny scroll tick
- [ ] The user can invoke a command to return to the previous position
- [ ] The command does not conflict with browser text-edit undo in input fields
- [ ] docs/keybindings.md documents the command if a keybinding is added

## Verification

Navigate several pages away, invoke the undo movement command, and confirm the viewport returns to the previous meaningful reading position.

title: Make more overlay controls Vimium-hintable
description:
## Context

The note "Make fingers select more things" points at Vimium F hints and clickable/selectable controls. Custom interactive controls must be real buttons or semantic elements to be discoverable.

## What to build

Audit overlay controls and document affordances that should be reachable through Vimium hints. Convert non-semantic clickable divs to buttons or add appropriate role/tabindex only where a native element is not viable.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Important overlay controls are reachable through Vimium F hints
- [ ] No inert decorative elements become noisy hint targets
- [ ] Keyboard/focus behavior remains coherent
- [ ] CLAUDE.md guidance remains accurate

## Verification

Open a converted PDF with Vimium enabled, press F, and confirm expected overlay controls receive hints.

title: Investigate KTN page-number discrepancy around Internet pages
description:
## Context

The notes mention a specific discrepancy: 1063 vs 1073 for "Internet" in KTN pensumbok. This likely relates to PDF page index vs printed page number mapping, outline entries, or extracted text positions.

## What to build

Find the relevant cached/local KTN PDF if available, reproduce the discrepancy, and determine whether it is a viewer bug, source-PDF page-label issue, or user-facing mapping confusion.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The relevant document is identified or the bead records that it is missing locally
- [ ] The 1063/1073 discrepancy is reproduced or ruled out
- [ ] The likely cause is documented
- [ ] A follow-up implementation bead is created if there is a general viewer bug

## Verification

Use the real cached/local KTN document and compare viewer page, printed page label, outline/search result, and browser find behavior for "Internet".

title: Explore visual block mode for PDF text selection
description:
## Context

The user is curious about a visual block mode. This is exploratory and should not be implemented as a full feature until the interaction model is clearly useful.

## What to build

Define a small experiment for rectangular/block-style selection in converted PDFs, including what problem it solves better than current visual mode. Do not ship a broad implementation without user review.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A concrete use case is written down
- [ ] The experiment defines commands and visual feedback
- [ ] The user approves whether this is worth implementing
- [ ] Follow-up implementation beads are created only after approval

## Verification

User reviews the proposed visual block mode interaction and either accepts, rejects, or parks it.

title: Redesign Command-Shift-Period surface as an information bar
description:
## Context

The current Command-Shift-Period UI is a tiny white bubble that stands out. The user mentioned an entire bar with document information, but also said this is out of scope for now and needs visual design thought.

## What to build

Create a design proposal for replacing the bubble with a quiet full-width or header-like bar that can include document information. Do not implement until the design is accepted.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The proposal explains what information belongs in the bar
- [ ] The proposal includes interaction states and when the bar appears/disappears
- [ ] The visual direction is consistent with the viewer style
- [ ] User review decides whether to implement

## Verification

User reviews the design proposal or mockup and decides whether this becomes an implementation bead.

title: Document PDF producer compatibility: xelatex vs pdflatex
description:
## Context

The user observes that xelatex-generated PDFs produce much better selectable text in the viewer, while pdflatex reports can look blurry or OCR-like. This may matter for future pdf2htmlEX integration or input guidance.

## What to build

Investigate a small set of xelatex and pdflatex PDFs, document which PDF features affect pdf2htmlEX extraction/rendering quality, and capture practical guidance for source PDFs.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Compare at least one xelatex and one pdflatex generated PDF if examples are available
- [ ] Identify whether the difference is fonts, embedded text, images, encoding, or another PDF feature
- [ ] Document practical guidance for producing viewer-friendly PDFs
- [ ] Create future engine-level beads if deeper pdf2htmlEX changes are warranted

## Verification

Run both sample PDFs through the viewer and compare selectable text, rendered clarity, and extracted DOM text.

title: Park future pdf2htmlEX, Vimium, and native app integration tracks
description:
## Context

The notes mention integrating with/forking pdf2htmlEX, rewriting it for arm64, forking Vimium, and eventually shipping a monolithic macOS menu bar app. The user explicitly framed these as future/out-of-scope for the current LLM-driven development pass.

## What to build

Capture the future architecture tracks in a short ADR candidate or roadmap note only when they become relevant. For now, prevent agents from treating these as immediate implementation tasks.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The future tracks are documented as out-of-scope for current beads
- [ ] No current task starts a pdf2htmlEX fork, Vimium fork, or native app rewrite without explicit user direction
- [ ] If future work begins, it starts with a design/research bead and ADR

## Verification

Review br ready and docs/ai-production.md to confirm current implementable work stays within the existing repo architecture.

title: Codify verification loops for agent work
description:
## Context

Before implementation agents start working through the Beads queue, they need an explicit verification contract and tool ladder.

## What to build

Document the available browser, Playwright, daemon, Comet/Raycast, and manual verification loops. Wire that into CLAUDE.md, README.md, and docs/ai-production.md so agents cannot close work without proof.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] docs/verification.md describes available verification surfaces
- [ ] docs/ai-production.md requires verification comments before close
- [ ] CLAUDE.md points agents to verification guidance
- [ ] README.md links the verification doc

## Verification

git diff --check, br agents --check, br sync --status.

title: Drain legacy TODO into Beads backlog
description:
## Context

TODO.md contains historical usage notes and feature ideas. New work should be tracked in Beads so agents can claim narrow slices.

## What to build

Convert each actionable TODO.md item into one or more beads with AFK/HITL labels, priorities, dependencies, and verification notes. Keep any non-actionable prose only as context.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Every actionable unchecked TODO.md item has a corresponding bead or is explicitly rejected in a bead note
- [ ] High-priority defects are not buried under roadmap ideas
- [ ] TODO.md is either empty of active tasks or links to the relevant bead IDs

## Verification

br list --status=open plus a final scan of TODO.md.
close_reason: Parsed current TODO/context dump into Beads under pdfv-yg1

title: Initialize page counter from visible page on launch
description:
## Context

The page number indicator can be stuck at 1 on launch until the user moves at least one page. This makes the viewer report the wrong location immediately after opening a document.

## What to build

Make the page counter compute and render the actual visible/current page during overlay initialization, before any scroll or page movement input happens.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Opening a converted PDF directly to a non-first-page restored position shows the correct page without requiring movement
- [ ] Opening at the first page still shows page 1
- [ ] The fix works with normal reload and hard reload
- [ ] No page-position cache is trusted until the DOM has enough information to compute current visibility

## Verification

Open a cached PDF through localhost:7435 at a restored/non-first-page position and confirm the page counter is correct before pressing any navigation key.

title: Stop Tab from changing pages
description:
## Context

Pressing Tab currently changes pages. The user does not want Tab to be a page navigation command in the viewer. Tab should preserve normal focus traversal or be safely ignored depending on the active surface.

## What to build

Find the Tab handler or browser-default interaction that causes page changes and remove that behavior without breaking semantic focus for overlay controls.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Pressing Tab in the document surface does not move to another page
- [ ] Pressing Tab inside menus/dialogs still follows useful focus behavior or is intentionally scoped
- [ ] docs/keybindings.md is updated if Tab is currently documented as a command

## Verification

Open a converted PDF, note the current page, press Tab repeatedly in the document surface, and verify the page does not change.

title: Prevent dragging the PDF background image while selecting text
description:
## Context

pdf2htmlEX leaves image/background layers behind the text. When the user starts near text but misses and hits the background, Chrome can drag the page image instead of behaving like a PDF text viewer.

## What to build

Make non-text PDF background/image layers non-draggable and non-interactive where appropriate, while preserving text selection and links.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Dragging on page whitespace or background does not start a browser image drag ghost
- [ ] Text can still be selected normally
- [ ] Links or intentional clickable elements still work
- [ ] The change is scoped to converted PDF page layers, not global browser behavior

## Verification

In a converted PDF, drag from whitespace near text and confirm no image drag starts; then select real text and click a real link if available.

title: Stop text selection from snapping to the top when dragged into whitespace
description:
## Context

When selecting text, moving the cursor into whitespace can cause the selection to extend unexpectedly up to the top of the page. The desired behavior is closer to a normal PDF/text viewer: missing text should not explode the selection range.

## What to build

Diagnose the text-layer geometry or selection event behavior that causes whitespace drags to anchor incorrectly, then constrain selection behavior so whitespace does not select unrelated earlier page text.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A repro case demonstrates the current whitespace-to-top selection jump
- [ ] Dragging slightly outside text no longer selects unrelated text at the top of the page
- [ ] Normal multi-line text selection still works
- [ ] The fix does not disable native text selection globally

## Verification

On a representative converted PDF, drag-select a sentence/paragraph and move the pointer into nearby whitespace; confirm the selection remains local.

title: Make copied/visible selections preserve spaces between words
description:
## Context

Selections can look or behave as if they are chopped at spaces. The underlying text segmentation may be necessary for browser find, but the user-facing selection/copy experience should preserve normal word spacing.

## What to build

Investigate whether the chopped selection is visual, clipboard text, DOM text segmentation, or CSS spacing. Improve the selection/copy surface so selected sentences behave as continuous text with spaces.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Reproduce a selection where spaces cause visibly or clipboard-chopped output
- [ ] Selected/copied text preserves spaces between words
- [ ] Native Cmd-F behavior is not regressed
- [ ] The change is documented if it relies on pdf2htmlEX DOM quirks

## Verification

Select and copy a sentence with spaces from a converted PDF, paste it into a plain text field, and verify normal spacing.

title: Prevent stale native-find selection from jumping the viewport back
description:
## Context

The overlay has custom selection-following behavior for marked/selected text. After native Cmd-F selects text, later scrolling and pressing Enter can reselect the old find result and jump the document back to that old location.

## What to build

Separate intentional overlay-driven selection movement from stale native browser find selection. The viewer should not unexpectedly jump back to an old find selection when the user is trying to continue reading or selecting elsewhere.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Reproduce the stale Cmd-F selection jump
- [ ] Pressing Enter after scrolling away does not resurrect an old find selection unless the browser find UI is actively being used
- [ ] Existing intentional selection auto-scroll behavior still works for active visual/mark workflows
- [ ] The boundary between native find and overlay selection handling is clear in code comments or docs if non-obvious

## Verification

Use Cmd-F to find text, scroll away, interact with selection/navigation, press Enter, and confirm the viewport does not jump back unexpectedly.
